questions.text: Soil erosion is one of the most serious threats to farming in many parts of Nigeria. Each year, heavy rains wash away the rich top layer of soil from farmlands, leaving behind land that can no longer support healthy crops. The problem is made worse when farmers clear forests and burn bushes, because the roots of trees hold the soil together and their leaves break the force of falling rain. Without this natural cover, rainwater runs swiftly over the surface, carrying soil into rivers and streams. The damage is not limited to farms. Eroded soil silts up rivers, making floods more likely and reducing the water available for drinking and irrigation. Fortunately, erosion can be controlled. Farmers can plant cover crops, build terraces on slopes, and practise contour ploughing. Communities that protect their forests and manage their land wisely will preserve the soil on which their livelihood depends. The passage is mainly about ___.
options: the dangers of soil erosion and how to control it
questions.explanation: The whole passage discusses the harm caused by erosion and the methods of controlling it.

questions.text: Many young Nigerians believe that farming is a job for the poor and the uneducated, and so they crowd into cities in search of white-collar jobs that are few and fiercely contested. This belief is both mistaken and costly. Modern agriculture is a business that rewards knowledge, planning and the use of technology, and it offers young people a faster route to self-reliance than years of waiting for employment that may never come. A graduate who starts a poultry farm or a vegetable garden with proper training can earn a steady income within months, while also creating jobs for others. Governments and banks have begun to support young farmers with loans and training, but the greatest obstacle remains the attitude of the youths themselves. Until farming is respected as a profession, the nation will continue to import food it could grow, and its young people will continue to chase jobs instead of creating them. The main argument of the passage is that ___.
options: young people should embrace modern agriculture
white-collar jobs are better than farming
graduates should not go into farming
questions.explanation: The passage argues throughout that youths should take up modern agriculture as a profession.

questions.text: Road accidents (1) ___ many lives in Nigeria every year. Most of these accidents are caused (2) ___ careless driving, over-speeding and poor vehicle maintenance. Drivers who obey traffic rules and (3) ___ their vehicles regularly are less likely to be involved in accidents. Passengers also have a duty: they should speak up when a driver (4) ___ recklessly. The Federal Road Safety Corps has continued to educate road users, but lasting safety will only come when every road user (5) ___ responsibility for his or her actions. Choose the word that best fills gap (1).
questions.explanation: The plural subject 'accidents' takes the plural verb form 'claim' in the present tense.

questions.text: Choose the option nearest in meaning to the word in quotes: The witness gave a 'candid' account of what happened.
questions.explanation: Candid means frank and honest.

questions.text: Choose the option nearest in meaning to the word in quotes: The manager remained 'adamant' despite all appeals.
questions.explanation: Adamant means refusing to change one's mind; unyielding.

questions.text: Choose the option nearest in meaning to the word in quotes: The old trader is 'frugal' with his earnings.
questions.explanation: Frugal means careful with money; thrifty.

questions.text: Choose the option nearest in meaning to the word in quotes: The meaning of the ancient poem is 'obscure'.
questions.explanation: Obscure means not clear or difficult to understand.

questions.text: Choose the option nearest in meaning to the word in quotes: She submitted a 'meticulous' report on the project.
questions.explanation: Meticulous means showing great attention to detail; thorough.

questions.text: Choose the option nearest in meaning to the word in quotes: The committee reached a 'unanimous' decision.
questions.explanation: Unanimous means agreed by everyone involved.

questions.text: Choose the option opposite in meaning to the word in quotes: The 'valiant' soldier defended the village.
questions.explanation: Valiant means brave, so its opposite is cowardly.

questions.text: Choose the option opposite in meaning to the word in quotes: The family lives in a 'spacious' apartment.
questions.explanation: Spacious means having plenty of room, so its opposite is cramped.

questions.text: Choose the option opposite in meaning to the word in quotes: Her remarks were 'ambiguous'.
questions.explanation: Ambiguous means open to more than one interpretation, so its opposite is clear.

questions.text: A place where birds are kept is called a(n) ___.
questions.explanation: An aviary is a place where birds are kept; an apiary is for bees and an aquarium is for fish.

questions.text: Choose the option nearest in meaning to the sentence: The student hardly ever comes late.
options: The student almost never comes late.
questions.explanation: 'Hardly ever' means almost never.

questions.text: The sentence 'Only the principal knows the truth' implies that ___.
options: the principal and others know the truth
no one else knows the truth
the truth is unknown to everyone
questions.explanation: 'Only' restricts the knowledge to the principal alone.

questions.text: Neither the teacher nor the students ___ present yesterday.
questions.explanation: With neither...nor, the verb agrees with the nearer subject, 'students', and the past tense is required by 'yesterday'.

questions.text: Each of the boys ___ a prize.
questions.explanation: 'Each' takes a singular verb, so 'has' is correct.

questions.text: The committee ___ decided to postpone the meeting.
questions.explanation: 'Committee' is treated here as a single body, so it takes the singular verb 'has'.

questions.text: One of the books ___ missing.
questions.explanation: 'One of' takes a singular verb, so 'is' is correct.

questions.text: By this time tomorrow, we ___ our examination.
questions.explanation: 'By this time tomorrow' requires the future perfect tense.

questions.text: They ___ football when it started to rain.
questions.explanation: An action in progress in the past takes the past continuous tense.

questions.text: I ___ my homework before my mother came home.
questions.explanation: The earlier of two past actions takes the past perfect tense.

questions.text: He has ___ here since 2020.
questions.explanation: The present perfect is used with 'since' for an action continuing from the past.

questions.text: If I ___ you, I would apologize.
questions.explanation: In unreal conditional sentences, 'were' is used after 'if I'.

questions.text: Choose the correct indirect speech: He said, 'I am busy today.'
options: He said that he is busy today.
He said that I am busy that day.
He said that he was busy today.
He said that he was busy that day.
questions.explanation: In reported speech, the present becomes past and 'today' becomes 'that day'.

questions.text: Choose the correct passive form: 'The boy kicked the ball.'
options: The ball was kicked by the boy.
The ball is kicked by the boy.
The ball has kicked by the boy.
questions.explanation: The passive of a past simple active sentence uses 'was' plus the past participle.

questions.text: Choose the correct question tag: 'She is coming, ___?'
questions.explanation: A positive statement takes a negative tag with the same auxiliary verb.

questions.text: Choose the correct reported question: She asked, 'Where do you live?'
options: She asked do I live where.
She asked where do I live.
questions.explanation: In reported questions, the word order returns to statement order and the tense shifts back.

questions.text: Choose the correctly spelt word from the options below.
questions.explanation: 'Occurrence' is spelt with double 'c' and double 'r'.

questions.text: Which of the following words is correctly spelt?
questions.explanation: 'Accommodate' is spelt with double 'c' and double 'm'.

questions.text: In the sentence 'The man whom you saw is my uncle', the clause 'whom you saw' is a(n) ___.
questions.explanation: The clause describes the noun 'man', so it is an adjectival (relative) clause.

questions.text: In 'Swimming is good exercise', the word 'Swimming' is a(n) ___.
questions.explanation: A verb form ending in -ing that functions as a noun is a gerund.

questions.text: To 'bite the dust' means to ___.
questions.explanation: To bite the dust means to fail or be defeated.

questions.text: To 'hit the nail on the head' means to ___.
questions.explanation: Hitting the nail on the head means saying exactly the right thing.

questions.text: A 'blessing in disguise' is ___.
options: an apparent misfortune that turns out well
questions.explanation: A blessing in disguise is an apparent misfortune that later turns out well.

questions.text: To 'let sleeping dogs lie' means to ___.
questions.explanation: Letting sleeping dogs lie means avoiding trouble by not reviving an old quarrel.

questions.text: Which word has the same vowel sound as 'seat'?
questions.explanation: 'Seat' and 'seed' both have the long /i:/ vowel sound.

questions.text: Which word has the same vowel sound as 'book'?
questions.explanation: 'Book' and 'look' both have the short /u/ vowel sound.

questions.text: Which word has the same vowel sound as 'coin'?
questions.explanation: 'Coin' and 'boy' both have the diphthong /oi/.

questions.text: Which word begins with the same consonant sound as 'church'?
questions.explanation: 'Church' and 'chair' both begin with the /tʃ/ sound.

questions.text: Which word ends with the same consonant sound as 'dogs'?
questions.explanation: 'Dogs' and 'beds' both end with the /z/ sound.

questions.text: Which word has the same consonant sound as the 'th' in 'think'?
questions.explanation: 'Think' and 'three' both have the voiceless /θ/ sound; the others have the voiced /ð/.

questions.text: Which word begins with the same consonant cluster as 'street'?
questions.explanation: 'Street' and 'stray' both begin with the three-consonant cluster /str/.

questions.text: Which word sounds the same as 'principal'?
questions.explanation: 'Principal' and 'principle' are homophones: they sound alike but differ in meaning and spelling.

questions.text: Which word is stressed on the first syllable?
questions.explanation: 'Teacher' is stressed on the first syllable, while the others are stressed on the second.

questions.text: Which word is stressed on the second syllable?
questions.explanation: 'Today' is stressed on the second syllable, while the others are stressed on the first.

questions.text: In answer to the question 'Did Ada buy the BAG?', the correct response with emphatic stress is ___.
options: No, Ada bought the bag YESTERDAY.
questions.explanation: The question challenges the object 'bag', so the emphasis falls on its replacement, 'shoe'.

questions.text: Which word rhymes with 'day'?
questions.explanation: 'Say' rhymes with 'day'.
